field_sources.model.image: B5 ImageGenClient's compiled-in Imagine model id. `features.image_gen_model_override` documents that an empty override 'defers to the remotely configured default', so this id is the binary's fallback, not a promise about which model served a given call.
field_sources.model.video: B4 `grok-imagine-video-1.5`, adjacent to video_gen/mod.rs in the binary; the same id in the vendor reference-to-video documentation. No `video_gen_model_override` knob exists, so this one is pinned by the CLI version.
field_sources.refs.max: D2 docs.x.ai multi-image editing: 'Use up to five source images for a single image edit.' B2 the CLI's own `image` schema states no cap, so five is the endpoint's documented limit rather than a CLI-verified one — hence verified_max false.
field_sources.aspects.generate: B1 ImageGenInput.aspect_ratio: "Aspect ratio of the generated image... Defaults to 'auto'. 1:1 for square (icons, profiles), 16:9 for wide (landscapes, cinematic), 9:16 for tall (phone wallpapers, stories), 3:2 for horizontal photos, 2:3 for vertical (portraits, posters)."
field_sources.aspects.edit: B2 ImageEditInput.aspect_ratio: 'Supported values: 1:1, 16:9, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4, 3:2, 2:3, 2:1, 1:2, 19.5:9, 9:19.5, 20:9, 9:20, auto.' The same string records that single-image edits ignore the parameter and keep the source ratio.
field_sources.exact_size: B1/B2 ImageGenInput has 2 fields and ImageEditInput 3; neither carries a resolution, size, or quality parameter. The Imagine REST API has them (D3), the CLI tools do not.
field_sources.transparent: B2 no alpha/background parameter on either tool; B5 the image client writes `jpg`. Alpha comes from share/image-chroma.sh keying a green plate.
field_sources.resume: B6 `-r/--resume <SESSION_ID_OR_TITLE>`; D1 headless documentation resumes by the `sessionId` reported on the terminal event.
field_sources.video.tools: B3 image_to_video 'Generate a video from a single source image'; reference_to_video 'Generate a video from reference images and/or preset voices, guided by a required text prompt'.
field_sources.video.refs_max: B3 reference_to_video.images: 'Reference images, up to 7 entries'; the runtime error '`images` must contain at most N image references.' guards it.
field_sources.video.voices_max: B3 reference_to_video.voices: 'up to 3 entries'; runtime error '`voices` must contain at most N preset voices.'
field_sources.video.voices: B3 the roster is not enumerated by the CLI: 'each a voice identifier from the built-in roster (e.g. "ara", "eve", "leo", "rex"; same voices as the xAI text-to-speech API; an unknown identifier fails with the list of available voices)'. null because no complete list is available offline; the four examples are the schema's own.
field_sources.video.durations: B3 image_to_video.duration: 'either 6 or 10 seconds. Default to 6 unless the user requests longer.'; runtime error '`duration` must be either 6 or 10 seconds.'
field_sources.video.reference_duration: B3 reference_to_video.duration: 'Duration of the video in seconds, between 1 and 15. Defaults to 6.'; B7 the bundled Imagine Video guidance repeats '`reference_to_video` accepts 1-15s'.
field_sources.video.resolutions: B3 both video tools: 'either 480p or 720p. Defaults to 480p'.
field_sources.video.aspects: B3 reference_to_video.aspect_ratio: '1:1 for square (icons, profiles), 16:9 for wide (landscapes, cinematic), 9:16 for tall (phone wallpapers, stories), 4:3 or 3:2 for horizontal photos, 3:4 or 2:3 for vertical (portraits, posters).' image_to_video has no aspect field at all (ImageToVideoInput has 4 elements: image, prompt, duration, resolution_name).
field_sources.video.container: B3 both tool descriptions point at `videos/1.mp4`; B5 the download client sends `video/mp4`.
field_sources.video.session_folder: B3 saved under the session's `videos/` folder, the video twin of `images/`.
field_sources.unsupported: B1/B2 no n/count ('To produce multiple images, emit multiple tool calls with distinct prompts'), no resolution, quality, seed, mask, response_format, or per-call model on either image tool; B3 image_to_video takes no aspect_ratio; B7 'Video starts from an image - there is no text-to-video tool.' D3 shows the REST API does expose n, resolution and quality, so their absence is a CLI limit rather than a model one.
